prompt: launch video for a note-taking app
great: Reasonable positioning even with missing details: avoids inventing specific features/numbers or flags them as placeholders; problem-solution-benefit arc, call to action.

plan.title: Meet Jotly: Never Lose an Idea Again
plan.description: Jotly is a note-taking app that helps you capture ideas fast and find them instantly. See how it works in three simple steps and how to get started.

beats.narration: You had a brilliant idea this morning. Where is it now? Scribbled on a receipt, buried in a chat, lost in a tab you closed. Your ideas deserve a better home.

props.title: Where did your idea go?
props.subtitle: Meet Jotly, the note-taking app that keeps your thoughts

beats.narration: Most of us keep notes in five places at once. A phone app, a paper pad, email drafts, sticky notes, and screenshots. Finding anything later becomes a treasure hunt nobody wins.
So we built Jotly, a note-taking app around one promise. Capture fast, find instantly, and never lose a thought again. Everything else follows from that single idea.

props.text: Capture fast. Find instantly. Never lose a thought.

beats.narration: Here is how it works in three steps. First, capture: type, speak, or snap a photo. Second, organize: Jotly suggests tags and folders for you. Third, find: search everything in seconds.

steps.label: Capture
steps.detail: Type, speak, or snap a photo

beats.narration: Everything flows the same way. Your ideas come in by typing, by voice, or as a photo. They all land in one notebook. Then search pulls up any note you need.
The benefits are simple. Speed, because a note opens in a blink. Sync, so your phone and laptop always match. Privacy, with a lock on any notebook. And links, connecting related ideas.
Before Jotly, notes are scattered, hard to search, and stuck on one device. After Jotly, they live in one place, searchable, and ready on every screen you own.
Good notes fit into real life. On a train, in a quiet cafe, between meetings. Jotly works offline too, and catches up the moment you reconnect.

props.alt: person working on a laptop at a coffee shop

beats.narration: Here is what you get. Offline mode. Voice notes. Photo capture. Fast search. Shared notebooks. Each one is built to keep you moving rather than slow you down.
Who is it for? A student studying in the library. A writer working at her desk. Anyone planning the week with a notebook full of ideas.

props.alt: People taking notes in different settings

beats.narration: We built Jotly on three beliefs. Notes should be quick to write. They should be easy to find. And they should always belong to you, never trapped behind a wall.
Getting started takes about a minute. Download the app, create your first notebook, and write one note. Import your old notes later, whenever you feel ready.
Because the best ideas rarely arrive at a convenient moment. They show up in the shower, on a walk, or just before sleep. Jotly is ready for all of them.

props.text: Your best ideas deserve to be found.

beats.narration: So stop chasing scraps of paper. Download Jotly today, write down one idea, and let it wait for you, safe and easy to find.

props.title: Download Jotly today
props.subtitle: Write down one idea. We will keep it safe.

accuracy.reason: The brief gave no product details, yet the script invents a full feature set (offline mode, voice notes, shared notebooks, per-notebook locks, AI-style tag suggestions) and states them as fact, without flagging placeholders.

coverage.reason: It has a problem, solution, benefit and CTA arc, but the features are generic and there is no differentiator, pricing or platform info.

structure.reason: The order is clear: problem, promise, how it works, benefits, audience, start, CTA. Beats 5, 7 and 9 repeat the capture/find/sync ideas.

hook_ending.reason: 'You had a brilliant idea this morning. Where is it now?' is a relatable hook, and the ending ('let it wait for you, safe and easy to find') closes cleanly with a CTA.

tone.reason: The voice is warm, conversational and suited to a consumer launch video.

visuals.reason: The scene types vary well (steps, diagram, versus, gallery, clip) and match the narration. There is no real product UI shown, and the checklist duplicates the earlier bullets.

originality.reason: Phrases like 'treasure hunt nobody wins' and 'one calm place' are stock launch-video language, and nothing is specific to this app.

instructions.reason: The length is roughly on target and it is a launch video. Because it invents a product name and features without flagging them as placeholders, it does not do what the reviewer's note asks.

language.reason: The English is clean, fluent and natural.

missing: Placeholders or flags for unspecified details such as price, platforms and the release date
A real differentiator against Evernote, Notion or Apple Notes
Social proof or a launch offer
A specific call-to-action URL or store names
wrong_facts: Unverified invented features: offline mode, voice notes, shared notebooks, notebook locks and tag suggestions were not in the brief.
judge.summary: This is a well-structured, fluent launch script with a clear problem-solution-CTA arc, but it is generic and asserts many invented features as fact. A stronger version would flag placeholders and offer a real differentiator.
